Ubud, Uluwatu cliffs, and rice terrace locations in Tegallalang are perennial favorites. Local crew talent is strong for camera and grip departments but thin for specialized VFX work. **Small / Medium scale** (alternative tier): Medium-Low risk. NIB + Standard Certificate issued **automatically**. Applies when the operation includes more complex service commitments.

**Large scale**: Medium-High risk. NIB + Standard Certificate within **14 working days**. Full documentation including TDUP and LSPr certification.

**PMA:** Fully open — 100% foreign ownership allowed.
59122.whatChanged: Direct match from KBLI 2020 (MATCH_LANGSUNG). Post-production keeps the same code and scope. No changes in the 2025 revision.
59122.baliContext: Bali's post-production scene is quietly growing. Several boutique VFX and editing houses operate from Canggu and Sanur, serving both local Indonesian productions and international clients remotely. The animation and motion graphics sub-sector is particularly active, with studios producing content for global streaming platforms. The key advantage: post-production is location-independent work that benefits from Bali's lower cost of living. Fast fiber internet (available in south Bali) is essential — check IndiHome or Biznet availability before signing a lease for your studio space.
59122.youllAlsoNeed:
- 59112 — Film/Video Production (if you also shoot original content)
- 59201 — Sound Recording (for audio post-production and mixing)
- 62192 — Digital Content Development (for interactive or app-based deliverables)
- 74194 — Game Content Design (if your VFX work extends to game cinematics)
59122.zantaraOpener: Setting up a post-production or VFX studio in Bali? 59122 covers editing, animation, and effects — and it's lower risk than production work.

59140.whatItMeans: Cinema operation — running movie theaters, screening rooms, and film exhibition venues. This covers traditional cinemas, boutique screening rooms, open-air movie nights, and drive-in theaters. The business is showing films to a paying audience, not making them. If you project it on a screen and sell tickets, this is the code.
59140.whatYouNeed:
**All scales (Micro / Small / Medium / Large)**: Low risk (Rendah). NIB only — no Standard Certificate required at any scale. This is unusually permissive for a public-facing entertainment venue. However, you still need a Building Feasibility Certificate (SLF) and fire safety compliance since you're hosting crowds in an enclosed space.

**PMA:** Fully open — 100% foreign ownership allowed.
59140.whatChanged: Direct match from KBLI 2020 (MATCH_LANGSUNG). Cinema operation is unchanged. Same code, same scope, same low-risk classification across all scales.
59140.baliContext: Traditional cinemas in Bali are dominated by the big chains (CGV, Cinepolis) in malls like Beachwalk and Park23. The real opportunity for foreign investors is in the boutique cinema / screening room niche — think curated film nights in Ubud, open-air screenings at resort venues, or private cinema experiences in villas. Bali's banjar system means noise and crowd management matter: get your neighbors on board before hosting outdoor screenings. The SLF (building certificate) process for public entertainment venues in Bali typically takes 1-3 months through the local DPMPTSP office.
59140.youllAlsoNeed:
- 59112 — Film Production (if you also produce original content for screening)
- 56301 — Bar (if you serve drinks during screenings)
- 56101 — Restaurant (if food service is part of the cinema experience)
- 93291 — Entertainment Venue (if hosting live events alongside screenings)
59140.zantaraOpener: Thinking about a cinema or screening venue in Bali? 59140 is low risk at every scale — but building safety compliance is the real gatekeep.

59201.whatItMeans: Sound recording and music publishing — running a recording studio, producing music, publishing songs, and distributing sound recordings. This also covers the 'aggregator' model: companies that act as intermediaries between independent artists and streaming platforms like Spotify or Apple Music. If you record it, publish it, or distribute it, this is the code.
59201.whatYouNeed:
**All scales (Micro / Small / Medium / Large)**: Low risk (Rendah). NIB only — no Standard Certificate required at any scale. This makes sound recording one of the most frictionless creative industry codes to set up. No TDUP needed (that's specific to film), no LSPr certification, no waiting periods.

**PMA:** Fully open — 100% foreign ownership allowed.
59201.whatChanged: Direct match from KBLI 2020 (MATCH_LANGSUNG). Sound recording and music publishing keep the same code and scope. No changes in the 2025 revision.
59201.baliContext: Bali has a surprisingly active music production scene. Studios in Canggu and Ubud cater to international artists recording in a tropical setting, and several music aggregator businesses operate from Bali serving Southeast Asian indie artists. The low-risk classification at all scales makes this an attractive entry point for creative entrepreneurs. Soundproofing is your main practical challenge — Bali's building standards don't account for studio acoustics, so budget for a proper build-out. The electronic music scene around Canggu creates natural demand for production and mastering services.
59201.youllAlsoNeed:
- 59112 — Film/Video Production (if you also produce music videos)
- 59122 — Post-Production (for audio post-production and mixing services)
- 58200 — Software Publishing (if you distribute via your own platform)
- 90001 — Performing Arts (if you also manage live performances)
59201.zantaraOpener: Starting a recording studio or music publishing company in Bali? 59201 is low risk at every scale — one of the easiest creative industry codes to launch.

60103.whatItMeans: On-demand audio distribution and streaming services — music streaming, audio podcasts, audiobooks. Covers subscription-based and ad-supported models. Includes both third-party content distribution and original content. Does NOT include traditional radio broadcasting (60101/60102).
60103.whatYouNeed:
**ALL scales: High Risk (Tinggi).** NIB + full License (Izin). Processing takes up to **29 working days** (7 admin + 15 technical inspection + 7 fee verification).

Requires: broadcasting plan (background, revenue projections, shareholding structure, coverage map, facilities), board members not blacklisted, multiple sworn statements (compliance, frequency licensing, content regulation), operational feasibility test, broadcasting license fee payment within 15 days.

**Authority:** Minister / Agency Head.

**PMA:** Fully open — 100% foreign ownership allowed.
60103.whatChanged: CODICE_RINUMERATO from KBLI 2020 code 60102 (Private Radio Broadcasting). The name change is significant — KBLI 2025 explicitly separates on-demand streaming from traditional broadcasting, recognizing the digital shift. However, the licensing requirements inherited from broadcasting are arguably over-regulated for pure streaming services.
60103.baliContext: The High Risk classification and broadcasting-era licensing requirements make this one of the most heavily regulated digital media codes. For a Bali-based podcast network or music streaming startup, the 29-day approval process and broadcasting infrastructure requirements (coverage maps, frequency licensing) are significant barriers. Most Bali-based audio content creators operate under general IT or content codes to avoid the broadcasting regulatory framework. The Kominfo PSE (Private Electronic System Provider) registration is also required.
60103.youllAlsoNeed:
- 59201 — Sound Recording (for original audio production)
- 63101 — Data Processing (for streaming infrastructure)
- 73100 — Advertising (if ad-supported model)
- 62199 — Software Development (for the streaming app)
60103.zantaraOpener: Launching an audio streaming platform in Indonesia? 60103 is your code — but brace yourself for High Risk broadcasting-era licensing requirements.

60390.whatItMeans: Social networking sites and content distribution/sharing platforms. Includes blogs, wikis, online gaming video sites, e-book distribution (non-publishing), and digital game intermediary services (vouchers, in-game items, premium access via marketplaces). A catch-all for social/sharing platforms.
60390.whatYouNeed:
**BPS_ONLY** — no PP28 risk assignment yet. Currently pending formal licensing framework. In practice, operators must register as PSE (Private Electronic System Provider) with Kominfo.

Likely will be classified as High Risk when PP28 integration occurs, given content moderation obligations.

**PMA:** Fully open — 100% foreign ownership allowed.
60390.whatChanged: BPS_ONLY — ENTIRELY NEW code in KBLI 2025. No direct predecessor. Previously social media platforms fell under web portal codes (63122) or were unclassified. The explicit inclusion of game item marketplaces and digital voucher sales is notable — Indonesia is acknowledging the digital goods economy.
60390.baliContext: The BPS_ONLY status makes this a 'watch and wait' code. Few Bali-based companies would build their own social media platforms, but the digital game marketplace provision is relevant for the gaming community. Content creators on existing platforms (YouTube, TikTok) do NOT need this code — it's for platform OPERATORS. The Kominfo PSE registration requirement applies regardless of PP28 status.
60390.youllAlsoNeed:
- 63101 — Data Processing (for platform infrastructure)
- 62199 — Software Development (for platform development)
- 73100 — Advertising (for ad revenue model)
- 62191 — E-Commerce App Development (if selling digital goods)
60390.zantaraOpener: Building a social platform or game marketplace? 60390 is Indonesia's new code for content distribution — still pending formal licensing requirements.

62110.whatItMeans: Technical development of video games — coding, engine creation, middleware, game software. Includes design/writing/testing/patching game code. Does NOT include game publishing (58211/58219) or game content design (74194).
62110.whatYouNeed:
**Small / Medium scale**: Medium-Low risk. NIB + Standard Certificate issued **automatically**. Must have SOP for after-sales service, competency training certificates, org chart with technical staff, guarantee no SARA content, age rating recommendations.

**Large scale**: Medium-High risk. NIB + Standard Certificate verified within **7 working days**. Needs staffing documentation (min 2 managers, 2 supervisors, 4 operational staff). Also has AI/blockchain sub-requirements (data governance annual report, SKKNI AI competency).

**PMA:** Fully open — 100% foreign ownership allowed. Authority: Bupati/Walikota (small/medium), Gubernur (large).
62110.whatChanged: MATCH_CON_AGGREGAZIONE from KBLI 2020 codes 62011, 62012, 62013, 62015, 62019. Previously game dev was bundled under general software programming. KBLI 2025 creates a dedicated code recognizing Indonesia's game industry as distinct.
62110.baliContext: Bali's game dev scene is small but growing, centered in Canggu coworking spaces. Most indie studios are 2-5 person teams. The IDR 10B PMA minimum makes this prohibitive for small studios — most operate as freelancers or use nominee structures. Denpasar Technopark has programs supporting game development. The key advantage of Bali is lifestyle + lower cost than Jakarta/Singapore, attracting remote game developers. However, fast internet is still inconsistent outside south Bali.
62110.youllAlsoNeed:
- 74194 — Game Content Design (art direction, level design, narrative)
- 58211 — Game Publishing (online distribution)
- 58219 — Other Game Publishing
- 62199 — Other Software Development (for non-game tools)
- 73100 — Advertising (if you market games directly)
62110.zantaraOpener: Building games from Bali? 62110 is your dedicated code for game development — let me explain the licensing and what changed in 2025.

Three distinct licensing tiers from aggregated PP28 sources (63121, 63111):

**Tier 1 — Kecil/Menengah**: Low risk (Rendah). NIB only, issued **automatically**. Validated Industrial Data reports every 6 months. Data security SOPs. HR competency training certificates. Authority: Bupati/Walikota.

**Tier 2 — Kecil/Menengah**: Medium-Low risk (Menengah Rendah). NIB + Standard Certificate, issued **automatically**. Same data reporting obligations plus: equipment calibration certificates, organizational structure documentation showing qualified technical staff, and safety/security guarantees for tools and processes. Authority: Bupati/Walikota.

**Tier 3 — Besar**: Medium-High risk (Menengah Tinggi). NIB + Standard Certificate within **7 days**. Requires: organizational chart with qualified staff, employment contracts for at least 2 managers + 2 supervisors + 4 technical staff (permanent or minimum 1-year contract), business process flow documentation, equipment list with photos. Authority: Gubernur.

**Post-issuance obligations (all tiers):**
- Submit validated Industrial Data every 6 months (Data Industri tervalidasi)
- Maintain SOPs for data and electronic system security (SOP keamanan data dan sistem elektronik)
- Obtain HR competency training certificates (sertifikat pelatihan kompetensi SDM)

63900.whatYouNeed:

**Small / Medium / Large scale**: Not listed in the risk data at these scales, which means Micro is the only explicitly mapped tier. In practice, if your operation grows beyond micro, expect the licensing authority to apply at minimum Medium-Low requirements.

64194.whatItMeans: Bank Perkreditan Rakyat (BPR) — Indonesia's rural/community bank providing basic banking services (savings, deposits, and credit) to local communities, SMEs, and individuals in their licensed geographic area. BPR cannot offer giro (checking accounts), cannot participate in national clearing, and cannot conduct international/foreign currency transactions — these are reserved for Umum banks. This is microfinance banking, not commercial banking. **TERBATAS (limited) foreign ownership: maximum 40% foreign shareholding.** Indonesian investors must hold at least 60%. OJK issues the BPR license — this is a full bank license process, not a standard OSS procedure.
64194.whatYouNeed:
**Risk: Tinggi.** The OSS process (NIB) is the administrative layer; the **OJK bank license is the operative requirement and takes 12–24 months.**

**Foreign ownership limit: maximum 40%.** This is a TERBATAS code — not fully open to PMA. Your Indonesian partner(s) must hold at least 60% of shares and be individuals or entities with proven financial capacity (fit & proper).

**Modal minimum by geographic category (per OJK POJK 5/2015 and updates):**
- **Wilayah Jabodetabek** (Jakarta Greater Area): IDR 16 miliar
- **Ibukota Provinsi** (Provincial capital, e.g., Denpasar): IDR 8 miliar
- **Kabupaten/Kota lain** (Other cities/regencies — most of Bali): IDR 6 miliar
- The entire capital must be paid up in full at time of OJK application

**TWO-PHASE process:**

**PHASE 1 — OSS / NIB:**
- Register PT (domestic structure required, since 60% must be Indonesian) on OSS
- Select 64194, Tinggi
- NIB issued; this does NOT authorize banking operations

**PHASE 2 — OJK BPR License (12–24 months):**
1. **Principle Approval (Izin Prinsip)** — initial OJK application showing founding shareholders, business plan, location; OJK evaluates feasibility (~3–6 months)
2. **Establishment (Pendirian)** — incorporate PT after Izin Prinsip; all shareholders must pass OJK fit & proper test
3. **Capital injection** — fully paid up in escrow; evidence submitted to OJK
4. **Physical premises** — OJK inspects the proposed office location; BPR cannot operate from virtual office
5. **Core Banking System** — OJK evaluates IT infrastructure; CBS must meet OJK POJK 75/2016 standards
6. **Director/Commissioner Fit & Proper** — OJK personally vets each director and commissioner
7. **Izin Usaha OJK** — issued after all stages clear; only then can BPR open to the public
8. **OJK ongoing supervision** — monthly financial reporting; annual audit by OJK-accredited auditor; Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) minimum 12%; NPL must not exceed 5%

**Geographic operational limit:** BPR may only operate within its licensed province. A Bali BPR cannot open branches in Java or Lombok without separate OJK approval.

**BPRS (Syariah) variant:** BPR Syariah follows sharia finance principles; governed by OJK and DSN-MUI; same capital requirements and foreign ownership limit of 40%.

**Typical full timeline:** 18–30 months from concept to first customer.
64194.whatChanged: Direct match from KBLI 2020 (MATCH_LANGSUNG). BPR was significantly restructured by **UU 4/2023 (P2SK Law)** which renamed BPR to 'Bank Perekonomian Rakyat' (keeping the same BPR acronym) and expanded the BPR product scope slightly. Key change: BPRs may now offer additional savings products and certain remittance services. The 40% foreign ownership cap is unchanged. OJK transferred BPR supervision fully from BI to OJK, which was completed in 2023.
64194.baliContext:
**🏦 BPR in Bali — The Microfinance Banking Layer**

**What BPR does that banks won't:**
- Provides loans of IDR 2–500 juta to UMKM operators, farmers, fishermen, village traders, and craftsmen who lack the collateral or documentation for commercial bank credit
- Accepts savings deposits from local community members (typically higher interest rate than bank savings, attracting local depositors)
- Processes faster than commercial banks — credit approval in 1–5 days vs 2–4 weeks for commercial bank SME loans

**Bali BPR landscape:**
- Bali has 130+ active BPRs (as of 2024) concentrated in Denpasar, Gianyar, Badung, and Tabanan
- Notable Bali BPRs: BPR Tish, BPR Dinar, BPR Sukawati Pancakanti (Gianyar focus), BPR Artha Hapat
- Competition is intense in south Bali; underpenetrated areas: Bangli, Karangasem (east Bali), Buleleng (north Bali)

**The 40% foreign + 60% Indonesian structure in practice:**
- Foreign investor contributes 40% equity (e.g., IDR 2.4 miliar of IDR 6 miliar minimum)
- Indonesian co-founder holds 60% (IDR 3.6 miliar) — must be a qualified individual or entity, not a nominee
- The Indonesian partner(s) must pass OJK fit & proper — no criminal record, no previous banking violations
- Common structure: experienced local Balinese banker (ex-BRI, ex-BNI) as 60% partner + foreign capital as 40% minority investor

**BPRS niche — halal microfinance for Middle Eastern tourism segment:**
- Bali receives increasing Middle Eastern and South Asian Muslim tourists
- A BPRS (Syariah) specifically serving halal-economy businesses (halal restaurants, Muslim-friendly homestays, abaya/modest fashion boutiques) = underexplored niche
- DSN-MUI sharia certification for products adds credibility

**⚠ Critical Issues**
- **40% cap is absolute** — OJK has rejected BPR applications where the foreign investor tried to exceed 40% through nominee structures; this is treated as fraud
- **Geographic restriction is real** — a Badung BPR cannot serve Ubud clients without opening a Gianyar branch (separate OJK approval); plan geographic scope from day one
- **NPL management is existential** — OJK places BPRs with NPL > 5% under enhanced supervision; NPL > 8% triggers OJK intervention; the BPR sector had 10+ forced mergers 2022–2024 due to NPL crises
64194.youllAlsoNeed:
- **64992** — Multifinance (if you want to add vehicle leasing or consumer goods financing to complement BPR micro-lending)
- **66191** — Fintech P2P Lending (for digital-first UMKM financing alongside the BPR physical branch model)
- **OJK legal counsel** — WAJIB — BPR license process requires specialized banking regulatory lawyer from Izin Prinsip through Izin Usaha; do not attempt without specialist legal support

Let me walk you through the Izin Prinsip process and what your Indonesian co-founder structure needs to look like.

64921.whatItMeans: Savings and loan cooperative (Koperasi Simpan Pinjam / KSP) — a member-owned financial cooperative that provides savings deposit facilities and credit/loans exclusively to its registered members. Only members can deposit; only members can borrow. This is structurally distinct from a bank (which serves the public) and from a multifinance company (which funds from capital markets). **CRITICAL: This code is TERTUTUP (closed) to foreign investment.** Only Indonesian legal entities and citizens (PMDN/WNI) may establish, own, or invest in a koperasi under Indonesian cooperative law. There is no PMA path into this structure. If your goal as a foreign investor is to serve the same underbanked UMKM market, your alternatives are: **66191** (fintech P2P lending, up to 85% foreign), **64992** (multifinance company, up to 85% foreign), or **64194** (BPR rural bank, up to 40% foreign).
64921.whatYouNeed:
**TERTUTUP — Foreign investment is not permitted under this code.**

This code is exclusively for Indonesian domestic entities (PMDN, WNI). The cooperative structure (badan hukum koperasi) is governed by UU 25/1992 (Perkoperasian) and cannot have foreign shareholders.

**For Indonesian founders (PMDN/WNI) establishing a KSP:**

Risk: Menengah Tinggi. Authority varies by geographic scope:
- **Bupati/Walikota** — for KSP operating within a single kabupaten/kota
- **Gubernur** — for KSP operating across multiple kabupaten within one province
- **Menteri** — for KSP operating across multiple provinces

Timeline: 7 working days for Sertifikat Standar (post-NIB).

**Steps for founding a KSP:**
1. **Founding meeting** — minimum 20 founding members required; draft AD/ART (anggaran dasar/rumah tangga)
2. **Notarial deed** — cooperative deed must be executed by a notaris
3. **Pengesahan Badan Hukum** — submission to Kemenkop UKM for legal entity approval (~30 days)
4. **NIB via OSS** — select 64921; risk Menengah Tinggi
5. **Sertifikat Standar** — submitted to Bupati/Walikota/Gubernur/Menteri depending on scope; 7 working day issuance
6. **OJK registration** — KSP that accept deposits above a threshold must register with OJK as LKNB (Lembaga Keuangan Non-Bank) under POJK 10/2016
7. **Operasional** — commence member recruitment, savings collection, and lending only after all permits are complete

**PMA alternatives (since 64921 is TERTUTUP):**
- **66191** — Fintech P2P lending (up to 85% foreign): technology-based lending platform connecting borrowers and lenders online; same UMKM financing gap, modern model
- **64992** — Multifinance (up to 85% foreign): vehicle leasing, UMKM working capital, property financing; IDR 100B minimum capital
- **64194** — BPR Rural Bank (maximum 40% foreign): traditional microbanking for local communities; OJK-licensed; IDR 6–16B minimum capital depending on location
64921.whatChanged: Direct match from KBLI 2020 (MATCH_LANGSUNG). The cooperative code and its TERTUTUP status for foreign investment are unchanged. The significant post-2020 development is OJK's expanded supervisory role over KSP following high-profile KSP collapses (KSP Indosurya 2020, KSP Sejahtera Bersama 2021) — OJK now requires larger KSPs to report financial data and comply with minimum liquidity ratios. For existing KSPs, this adds compliance burden.
64921.baliContext:
**🤝 The Indonesian Cooperative Landscape (Context for Foreign Investors)**

**Why this code matters to understand even if you can't use it:**
- Indonesia has 130,000+ registered cooperatives, of which ~20,000 are KSP; they collectively serve ~28 million member-borrowers
- KSP serves the UMKM segment that commercial banks won't touch: small traders, artisans, farmers, fishermen, temple offering sellers
- In Bali, the traditional Lembaga Perkreditan Desa (LPD) — Bali's unique village-level financial institution — operates alongside KSP serving the same base (LPD is actually NOT covered by KBLI 64921 — it has its own Perda Bali framework)
- The KSP sector in Indonesia has a troubled regulatory track record: several large KSPs (Indosurya IDR 15T, Sejahtera Bersama) collapsed under fraudulent management, wiping out millions of member savings

**The opportunity this points to for PMA investors:**
The gap that KSP serves — small loans (IDR 1–50 juta) for UMKM that commercial banks won't serve — is precisely where fintech P2P lending (66191) is growing fastest. If you want to serve Bali's 500,000+ UMKM operators (warungs, craftsmen, villa support businesses), P2P lending under 66191 is the legal PMA path.

**Bali LPD note:** The Lembaga Perkreditan Desa is a village-level financial institution unique to Bali, governed by Perda Bali No. 3/2017 — it is NOT a koperasi and NOT governed by KBLI 64921. Foreign investment in LPDs is similarly not permitted.
64921.youllAlsoNeed:
- **66191** — Fintech P2P Lending (primary PMA alternative to KSP for UMKM financing)
- **64992** — Multifinance/Perusahaan Pembiayaan (PMA alternative with vehicle leasing + working capital)
- **64194** — BPR Rural Bank (PMA alternative with max 40% foreign, OJK-licensed banking)
- **OJK legal counsel** — any financial services activity in Indonesia requires specialized regulatory legal advice; Kepmen 228/2019 and OJK regulations change frequently
64921.zantaraOpener: Koperasi Simpan Pinjam? This code is TERTUTUP — no foreign investment allowed. But if your goal is reaching Indonesia's underbanked UMKM market, I'll show you the three PMA paths that actually work: P2P lending (66191), multifinance (64992), and rural banking (64194).

64992.whatItMeans: Perusahaan Pembiayaan (multifinance company) — a non-bank financial institution that provides financing for: vehicle purchases (motor credit, car leasing), consumer goods, working capital for SMEs, property down payments, and factoring/receivables purchasing. Unlike a bank, a multifinance company cannot accept public deposits — it funds its portfolio from equity capital and bond issuance. Unlike P2P lending, it uses its own capital to extend credit (not matching borrowers with lenders). **Maximum foreign ownership: 85%** under OJK regulation (15% must be Indonesian). OJK governs under POJK 35/2018 (Penyelenggaraan Usaha Perusahaan Pembiayaan).
64992.whatYouNeed:
**Risk: Menengah Tinggi.** Authority: **Menteri** (OSS). OSS timeline 7 working days — but the OJK multifinance license is the critical gate (6–12 months).

**TWO-PHASE licensing — both mandatory:**

**PHASE 1 — OSS / NIB (7 working days):**
- Register PT PMA on OSS, select 64992, Menengah Tinggi
- NIB + Sertifikat Standar issued
- **Cannot extend financing to any customer without OJK license**

**PHASE 2 — OJK Multifinance License (POJK 35/2018) — 6–12 months:**
1. **Application to OJK** — Departemen Pengawasan IKNB I
2. **Minimum paid-up capital: IDR 100 miliar** — fully paid up at time of OJK application; largest minimum capital requirement in this session's codes
3. **Shareholders fit & proper test** — OJK vets all shareholders owning ≥ 25% and all directors/commissioners
4. **Business plan** — 5-year financial projections; portfolio composition (pembiayaan investasi, modal kerja, multiguna — each requires separate OJK approval of activities)
5. **IT infrastructure assessment** — OJK reviews loan origination system, credit scoring methodology, collections system
6. **Capital adequacy ratio:** OJK minimum gearing ratio (ratio modal terhadap pembiayaan) — typically multifinance must maintain minimum capital adequacy per POJK 35/2018
7. **OJK Izin Usaha** — issued after all stages pass
8. **Product-specific approvals** — each financing activity type (vehicle, property, multiguna) requires separate OJK product registration

**Step-by-step for PT PMA multifinance:**
1. **Establish PT PMA** — 85% foreign max, 15% Indonesian; notary deed, AHU (~4–6 weeks)
2. **Capital injection** — IDR 100 miliar fully paid up into Indonesian bank account (note: this is 4x larger than P2P lending requirement)
3. **NIB via OSS** — 64992, 7 working days
4. **OJK license application** — full dossier submission including business plan, credit policy, risk management framework, collections policy, IT system documentation
5. **OJK review and assessment** — includes site visit to office, interview with directors
6. **OJK Izin Usaha** — issued (~6–12 months from application)
7. **First financing transaction** — can commence immediately after Izin Usaha
8. **OJK ongoing reporting** — monthly financial reports; quarterly asset quality reports; annual audited financial statements

**Permitted financing activities (must be specified in OJK application):**
- **Pembiayaan Investasi** — productive assets: vehicle purchase (motor/mobil), machinery, equipment
- **Pembiayaan Modal Kerja** — working capital loans for SMEs
- **Pembiayaan Multiguna** — multi-purpose consumer financing
- **Sewa Pembiayaan (Finance Lease)** — asset leasing with option to purchase
- **Anjak Piutang (Factoring)** — purchasing receivables from vendors/sellers
- **KPA Bridging** — property down-payment financing (Kredit Pemilikan Apartemen bridging)

**Minimum total capital:** IDR 100 miliar paid-up — the highest capital requirement in this session.
**Maximum foreign ownership:** 85% (OJK POJK 35/2018); 15% Indonesian mandatory.
64992.whatChanged: Direct match from KBLI 2020 (MATCH_LANGSUNG). Key regulatory development: **OJK POJK 35/2018** (replacing POJK 29/2014) tightened capital adequacy requirements, added stronger consumer protection provisions, and introduced the distinction between pembiayaan investasi, modal kerja, and multiguna. Post-2022, OJK has increased scrutiny of multifinance NPL ratios following elevated defaults in motorcycle financing. OJK also imposed tighter debt-to-equity gearing limits (Net Gearing Ratio maximum 10x paid-up capital).
64992.baliContext:
**🚗 Multifinance in Bali — The Vehicle and Tourism Financing Market**

**The macro opportunity:**
- Indonesia's multifinance market: IDR 400+ triliun in receivables annually; dominated by Adira Finance (Astra group), BFI Finance, Mandiri Tunas Finance (bank-backed)
- Vehicle financing is the dominant product: Indonesia buys 6+ million motorcycles/year; Bali's tourism economy requires constant fleet renewal for motorbike rental companies, villa transport services, and tour operators

**The Bali-specific niches for a boutique PMA multifinance:**
- **Tourism fleet leasing:** Hotel and resort vehicle fleets (transport vans, minibuses, shuttle services) need finance lease arrangements; the asset is the collateral, appealing for Indonesian SME operators who lack land collateral for bank loans
- **Villa developer bridging:** Small villa developers (IDR 2–8B projects) need equity bridge financing for 12–24 months between construction start and villa sale; banks don't serve this size; P2P doesn't provide the right structure; a multifinance pembiayaan investasi product fills the gap
- **UMKM working capital — hospitality supply chain:** Restaurants, souvenir producers, food vendors need working capital advance against purchase orders from resorts; factoring/anjak piutang is the ideal product
- **Motorbike leasing for villa staff:** Villa and hotel staff who need motorbike transportation but can't qualify for bank consumer loans — high volume, small ticket, standardized credit scoring

**The IDR 100B capital reality:**
- IDR 100 miliar is ~USD 6.5 million — a meaningful commitment
- This filters out undercapitalized entrants and signals genuine intent to OJK
- For a 10x gearing ratio (max), IDR 100B capital supports IDR 1 triliun in financing portfolio — a significant operation

**⚠ Critical Issues**
- **NPL management is the business** — multifinance profitability depends entirely on credit quality; Bali's tourism economy is seasonal (NPL spikes in low season Oct–Mar as borrowers' cash flow weakens); build seasonal cash flow into credit underwriting
- **Gearing ratio ceiling** — maximum Net Gearing Ratio of 10x means your financing portfolio is capped at IDR 1T for IDR 100B capital; scaling beyond requires additional capital injection or bond issuance
- **Collections in Bali** — Indonesia's collections culture for consumer finance requires physical presence; motorbike repossession requires Fidusia (fiduciary lien registration at KEMENKUMHAM) before any collateral can be repossessed legally; skip this step and you lose all collateral rights
- **Fidusia registration** — every secured financing transaction must be registered with the Fiduciary Office (Kemenkumham) within 30 days; failure = criminal violation; factor registration cost (~IDR 50K per contract) into pricing
64992.youllAlsoNeed:
- **66191** — Fintech P2P Lending (digital lending complement for smaller ticket UMKM loans below multifinance minimum)
- **64194** — BPR Rural Bank (physical branch micro-lending alongside multifinance operations)
- **52101** — Warehousing (for vehicle repossession storage and fleet management)
- **OJK legal counsel** — WAJIB — multifinance license application, POJK 35/2018 compliance, Fidusia registration framework; requires specialist IKNB legal expertise
64992.zantaraOpener: Multifinance company in Bali — vehicle leasing, villa developer bridging, or UMKM working capital? 64992 is the code: 85% max foreign, OJK license required, IDR 100B minimum capital (the highest in the fintech/finance sector). The Bali tourism fleet leasing and hospitality supply chain factoring niches are genuinely underserved. Let me walk you through the OJK process and what IDR 100B actually buys you.

65121.whatItMeans: General insurance (non-life insurance) — providing insurance coverage for property, motor vehicles, marine cargo, fire, liability, health (group), travel, and other short-term risks. This covers all conventional non-life insurance products: car insurance, property insurance for villas/hotels, marine cargo insurance for shipments, travel insurance for tourists, group health insurance for companies. Policies are typically annual contracts renewed yearly. This is NOT life insurance (65111) or syariah insurance (65211) — this is conventional general insurance.
65121.whatYouNeed:
**BPS_ONLY code** — no `per_skala` data in KBLI 2025 JSON. The OSS licensing pathway shows: Risk: Tinggi (High). Authority: **Menteri/Kepala Badan** (ministerial level). Kewajiban: **Berbentuk badan hukum** (must be legal entity).

**Critical: NIB is NOT the insurance license**
The NIB from OSS is only the legal business entity registration. The actual insurance operating license comes from **OJK** (Otoritas Jasa Keuangan / Financial Services Authority) under **UU 40/2014** (Perasuransian / Insurance Law).

**Two-stage licensing process:**

**Stage 1: PT PMA Establishment + NIB**
1. **PT PMA incorporation** — notary deed, AHU registration; minimum IDR 10B stated capital (~3–5 weeks)
2. **NIB via OSS** — register on oss.go.id, select 65121, Tinggi path; NIB issued (~2–3 days)
3. **Kewajiban compliance** — "Berbentuk badan hukum" satisfied by PT PMA structure

**Stage 2: OJK Insurance License (Izin Usaha Perasuransian)**
4. **OJK application** — submit to OJK for Izin Usaha as general insurer
5. **Modal disetor minimum** — **IDR 100 billion** paid-up capital for new general insurance company (POJK requirement, far higher than PT PMA minimum)
6. **Fit & proper test** — all directors, commissioners, and controlling shareholders must pass OJK fit & proper assessment
7. **Business plan submission** — detailed actuarial projections, reinsurance arrangements, risk management framework
8. **Reinsurance treaty** — must have reinsurance agreements in place before OJK approval
9. **OJK approval timeline** — **6–18 months** from application to license issuance (highly variable depending on completeness)

**Post-license obligations:**
- Quarterly financial reporting to OJK
- Solvency margin compliance (Risk-Based Capital / RBC minimum 120%)
- Annual actuarial review and audit
- Consumer protection compliance (POJK 1/2013)

**Typical total timeline:** 12–24 months from PT PMA to operational insurance company (OJK license is the bottleneck).
**Minimum capital:** IDR 100 billion paid-up (OJK requirement) + IDR 10B PT PMA stated capital.

**Authority:** Menteri/Kepala Badan (OSS) + OJK (insurance license).
**PMA:** Historically 80% cap on foreign ownership for **acquisitions** of existing insurers. For **new establishment**, check current Perpres — PMA percentage may be limited. Verify with OJK before proceeding.
65121.whatChanged: General insurance existed in KBLI 2020 under similar codes. KBLI 2025 maintains the classification as BPS_ONLY, meaning detailed per-scale licensing data is not yet fully defined in OSS. The core regulatory framework remains OJK-based under UU 40/2014, unchanged from previous years.
65121.baliContext:
**🏝 General Insurance in Bali (Active Market, High Barriers to Entry)**
- Bali has significant demand for general insurance: property insurance for villas/hotels (fire, earthquake, flood), motor vehicle insurance (massive market — millions of vehicles), marine cargo insurance (Benoa port shipments), travel insurance for tourists
- **Existing players dominate:** Major Indonesian insurers (Asuransi Astra, Sinar Mas, Allianz Indonesia, ACA, Zurich) already have strong distribution in Bali
- **Expat market:** International health insurance plans (CIGNA, AIA, Allianz) serve expat community; group health insurance for companies is a growing segment

---

**💡 PMA Opportunities (Realistic Assessment)**
- **Establishing a new general insurer is extremely difficult:** IDR 100B capital requirement, 12–24 month OJK approval process, intense competition from established players
- **More practical path: Insurance agency (66221)** — act as intermediary selling insurance products on behalf of existing insurers; much lower capital requirement (IDR 10B PT PMA only), faster licensing, immediate revenue
- **Niche opportunities:** Specialty insurance for tourism sector (villa rental insurance, tour operator liability, event cancellation), marine insurance for yacht/boat owners, expat health insurance brokerage
- **Acquisition route:** Buying an existing small general insurer may be faster than new establishment, but PMA cap (historically 80% for acquisitions) applies — verify current regulations

---

**⚠ Critical Points for Foreign Investors**
- **OJK license is separate and mandatory:** Do not assume NIB = permission to operate insurance business; OJK Izin Usaha is the critical license
- **IDR 100B capital is real:** This is paid-up capital, not stated capital; you must actually deposit IDR 100 billion into the company bank account
- **Fit & proper test is strict:** OJK will reject directors/commissioners with poor financial history, criminal records, or insufficient insurance industry experience
- **Reinsurance is mandatory:** General insurers must have reinsurance treaties to manage risk; this requires relationships with international reinsurers
- **Consider agency model first:** 66221 (insurance agent) is a much more accessible entry point into Bali's insurance market — test the market before committing IDR 100B to a new insurer
65121.youllAlsoNeed:
- **66221** — Insurance agent — if you want to sell insurance products without establishing a full insurer (much lower capital requirement)
- **66222** — Insurance broker (pialang) — if you want to represent clients and place insurance with multiple insurers
- **64191** — Banking services — if you offer bancassurance products through bank partnerships
- **74100** — Business consulting — if you provide risk management consulting alongside insurance products
65121.zantaraOpener: Establishing a general insurance company in Bali? 65121 is the code, but the reality is tough: IDR 100 billion capital, 12–24 month OJK approval, intense competition. Most foreign investors find 66221 (insurance agent) a more practical entry point. Let me explain both paths.

66125.whatItMeans: Money changer (foreign exchange services) — buying and selling foreign currencies and traveler's cheques at physical exchange counters. This is the classic money changer business model: tourists and locals exchange USD, EUR, AUD, SGD, JPY, CNY for Indonesian Rupiah (and vice versa). Physical counter operations, not digital/fintech forex trading. This code covers authorized money changing activity regulated by Bank Indonesia, distinct from unauthorized/illegal money changers.
66125.whatYouNeed:
**Risk: Tinggi (High). Authority: Menteri/Kepala Badan. Timeline: Otomatis (NIB auto-issued). Kewajiban: Berbentuk badan hukum.**

**Critical: This is Bank Indonesia (BI) regulated, NOT OJK**
Money changing falls under **Bank Indonesia** jurisdiction, not OJK. The regulatory framework is **PBI 18/20/PBI/2016** (Kegiatan Usaha Penukaran Valuta Asing Bukan Bank / KUPVA-BB).

**Two-stage licensing process:**

**Stage 1: PT PMA Establishment + NIB**
1. **PT PMA incorporation** — notary deed, AHU registration; minimum IDR 10B stated capital (~3–5 weeks)
2. **NIB via OSS** — register on oss.go.id, select 66125, Tinggi path; NIB auto-issued (Otomatis) (~2–3 days)
3. **Kewajiban compliance** — "Berbentuk badan hukum" satisfied by PT PMA structure

**Stage 2: Bank Indonesia KUPVA-BB License**
4. **BI application** — submit to Bank Indonesia for KUPVA-BB (Kegiatan Usaha Penukaran Valuta Asing Bukan Bank) license
5. **Modal disetor minimum** — **IDR 500 million** paid-up capital (much lower than OJK financial products)
6. **Location requirements** — physical office/counter in commercial area, tourism zone, or airport; BI inspects premises before approval
7. **KYC/AML systems** — must have Know Your Customer and Anti-Money Laundering procedures in place (BI regulation)
8. **Exchange rate transparency** — must display BI-approved exchange rates prominently; rate manipulation is prohibited
9. **BI approval timeline** — **2–6 months** from application to license issuance

**Post-license obligations:**
- Display BI license prominently at counter (mandatory)
- Daily transaction reporting to BI for transactions > IDR 100 million
- KYC documentation for large transactions (passport copy, transaction purpose)
- Exchange rate posting (buy/sell rates must be visible to customers)
- Annual audit and BI inspection compliance

**Typical total timeline:** 3–8 months from PT PMA to operational money changer (BI license + premises setup).
**Minimum capital:** IDR 500 million paid-up (BI requirement) + IDR 10B PT PMA stated capital.

**Authority:** Menteri/Kepala Badan (OSS) + Bank Indonesia (KUPVA-BB license).
**PMA:** Fully open (Terbuka) — 100% foreign ownership.

66151.whatItMeans: Investment advisory services — providing professional advice on investments in securities, portfolio management recommendations, financial planning, and wealth management advisory. This is advisory-only service: you analyze investments, recommend strategies, provide financial planning, but you do NOT directly manage client funds or execute trades. That's the key distinction from asset management (66111, Manajer Investasi) — advisory gives advice, asset management executes and manages. Common services: portfolio analysis, asset allocation recommendations, retirement planning, tax-efficient investment strategies, wealth preservation consulting.
66151.whatYouNeed:
**Risk: Tinggi (High). Authority: Menteri/Kepala Badan. Timeline: Otomatis (NIB auto-issued). Kewajiban: Berbentuk badan hukum.**

**Critical: This is OJK regulated — separate license required**
Investment advisory falls under **OJK** (Otoritas Jasa Keuangan) jurisdiction. The regulatory framework is **POJK 10/2012** (Wakil Manajer Investasi dan Penasihat Investasi).

**Two-stage licensing process:**

**Stage 1: PT PMA Establishment + NIB**
1. **PT PMA incorporation** — notary deed, AHU registration; minimum IDR 10B stated capital (~3–5 weeks)
2. **NIB via OSS** — register on oss.go.id, select 66151, Tinggi path; NIB auto-issued (Otomatis) (~2–3 days)
3. **Kewajiban compliance** — "Berbentuk badan hukum" satisfied by PT PMA structure

**Stage 2: OJK Investment Advisory License (Izin Penasihat Investasi)**
4. **OJK application** — submit to OJK for Izin Penasihat Investasi
5. **Modal disetor minimum** — **IDR 200 million** paid-up capital (much lower than asset management which requires IDR 25 billion)
6. **Individual advisor licenses** — all advisors must hold **WPI** (Wakil Penasihat Investasi) license from OJK; requires passing OJK exam
7. **Fit & proper test** — directors and commissioners must pass OJK fit & proper assessment
8. **Compliance infrastructure** — AML/CFT procedures, client suitability assessment framework, conflict of interest policies
9. **Professional indemnity insurance** — required to protect clients from advisory errors
10. **OJK approval timeline** — **3–6 months** from application to license issuance

**Post-license obligations:**
- Quarterly reporting to OJK on client numbers, assets under advisory
- Annual compliance audit
- Client suitability documentation (must assess client risk profile before giving advice)
- Disclosure of conflicts of interest (e.g., commissions from product providers)
- Continuing professional education for WPI license holders

**Typical total timeline:** 4–8 months from PT PMA to operational advisory firm (OJK license + WPI certifications).
**Minimum capital:** IDR 200 million paid-up (OJK requirement) + IDR 10B PT PMA stated capital.

**Authority:** Menteri/Kepala Badan (OSS) + OJK (investment advisory license).
**PMA:** Fully open (Terbuka) — 100% foreign ownership.

66191.whatItMeans: Financial technology peer-to-peer (P2P) lending platform — a technology-based marketplace that connects borrowers directly with individual or institutional lenders, without a bank as intermediary. The platform earns fees (not interest) from facilitating the loan matching. Products include: consumer loans (personal, salary-based), productive/UMKM loans, invoice financing, and crowdfunding-style project financing. This is one of the most heavily regulated fintech activities in Indonesia — OJK's POJK 10/2022 governs every aspect of operations. **Maximum foreign ownership: 85%** (15% must be held by Indonesian shareholders under POJK 10/2022).
66191.whatYouNeed:
**Risk: Tinggi (High).** Authority: **Menteri** (via OJK). NIB via OSS is 14 working days — but this is only the beginning. The OJK license is the critical gate that takes 6–12 months on top of the OSS process.

**TWO-PHASE licensing — both are mandatory:**

**PHASE 1 — OSS / NIB (14 working days):**
- Register PT (or PT PMA) on OSS, select 66191, Tinggi path
- NIB + Izin issued after government verification
- **This alone does NOT authorize you to operate** — it is administrative registration only

**PHASE 2 — OJK P2P Lending License (POJK 10/2022) — 6–12 months:**
1. **OJK Sandbox (optional but recommended for new models):** Apply for OJK Regulatory Sandbox (12-month pilot); allows testing under relaxed rules before full licensing
2. **Izin Usaha OJK application** — submitted to OJK Departemen Pengawasan IKNB II
3. **Minimum paid-up capital:** IDR 25 miliar fully paid up at time of OJK application; must be evidenced by bank statement from Indonesian bank
4. **Fit & proper test** — OJK vets all directors and commissioners individually; clean criminal record, no previous financial sector violations
5. **Sistem IT assessment** — OJK reviews platform architecture, data security, anti-fraud systems, server location (must be in Indonesia, PP 71/2019)
6. **Document submission:** Articles of incorporation, business plan, financial projections (5-year), risk management policy, credit scoring methodology, KYC/AML procedures, partnership agreements (if any), OJK questionnaire
7. **OJK interview** — senior management must attend regulatory interview
8. **OJK Izin Usaha** — issued only after all above steps pass; without this, you cannot onboard a single borrower or lender

**Step-by-step full path for PT PMA P2P fintech:**
1. **Establish PT PMA** — minimum 85% foreign, 15% Indonesian; notary deed, AHU, TDP (~4–6 weeks)
2. **Capital injection** — IDR 25 miliar into Indonesian PT bank account
3. **NIB via OSS** — 66191, Tinggi; 14 working days
4. **Technology platform development** — build/acquire the lending platform (if not already built); ensure data localization compliance (all borrower data on Indonesian servers)
5. **OJK license application** — file complete dossier; average processing 6–12 months
6. **OJK approval + Izin Usaha** — issued after all assessments pass
7. **Bank/escrow account setup** — loan funds must flow through OJK-designated escrow or virtual account bank partners
8. **Commence operations** — first borrower/lender onboarding

**Operational constraints under POJK 10/2022:**
- **Interest rate caps:** Consumer loans max 0.4%/hari; productive/UMKM loans max 0.1%/hari
- **Borrower cap:** Individual borrower max IDR 2 miliar outstanding across all P2P platforms
- **Lender reporting:** Lenders classified as retail or institutional; institutional lenders must be OJK-registered
- **Non-performing loan (NPL) threshold:** OJK monitors NPL ratio; platforms exceeding limits face enhanced supervision
- **Advertising restrictions:** Cannot advertise guaranteed returns to lenders

**Minimum total capital (operational):** IDR 25 miliar paid-up at application; must maintain minimum capital adequacy throughout operations.
**Minimum foreign participation:** Up to 85% foreign allowed; 15% Indonesian mandatory.
**Typical full timeline:** 12–18 months from incorporation to first loan disbursement.
66191.whatChanged: This code was significantly transformed by **POJK 10/2022** (Peraturan OJK No. 10/POJK.05/2022), which replaced the previous POJK 77/2016. Key changes: raised minimum capital from IDR 2.5 miliar to IDR 25 miliar; tightened foreign ownership to maximum 85%; introduced daily interest rate caps; strengthened escrow/virtual account requirements; and expanded OJK supervisory powers including the ability to immediately revoke licenses for violations. The KBLI code (66191) is unchanged from KBLI 2020, but the regulatory substance changed dramatically.
66191.baliContext:
**📱 FinTech P2P Lending in Bali — The Opportunity and the Reality**

**The national market:**
- Total P2P lending outstanding: IDR 60+ triliun (2023); 100+ registered/licensed platforms
- Major incumbents: Kredivo (consumer), Modalku (UMKM), Investree (SME invoice), Akseleran (UMKM), Akulaku (consumer)
- OJK registered platforms: ~100 (down from 170+ pre-consolidation; OJK revoked licenses aggressively 2022–2023)

**The Bali-specific niche:**
- **Tourism UMKM working capital:** Villa managers, restaurant operators, and souvenir vendors need short-term working capital loans between tourist seasons; traditional banks won't serve them below IDR 50M
- **Hospitality worker salary advance:** Hotel and villa staff (low salary, irregular income) are prime P2P consumer loan targets — they have employment verification but low credit scores
- **Villa developer bridging finance:** Small developers (IDR 2–5B projects) need bridging loans that neither BPR nor commercial banks provide efficiently
- **Craft export financing:** Gianyar craftsmen who receive foreign buyer orders need advance finance for materials and production

**Why the barrier is high:**
- IDR 25B minimum capital is a real filter — it eliminates casual entrants
- The OJK 6–12 month licensing process requires a dedicated compliance team from day one
- Building an NPL-controlled loan portfolio in a market dominated by experienced Indonesian players requires genuine credit scoring innovation

**⚠ Critical Compliance Traps**
- **Data localization is absolute** — borrower and transaction data must reside on servers physically located in Indonesia; using AWS Singapore or Google Hong Kong is a violation
- **Virtual account partner requirement** — OJK requires funds to flow through a licensed bank's virtual account (VA) system, not directly from lender to borrower; partner banks for this service charge meaningful fees
- **OJK SPRINT reporting** — all active P2P platforms must report loan disbursements, collections, and NPL data to OJK's SPRINT system in near-real-time
- **License revocation history** — OJK revoked 100+ P2P licenses 2022–2024 for capital inadequacy, NPL threshold breaches, and data violations; treat OJK compliance as existential, not administrative

66199.whatItMeans: Other financial services not elsewhere classified — the catch-all for financial activities outside the specific banking, insurance, and capital markets codes. This code covers a wide range of activities, each with its own regulator: payment gateways, e-money issuers, money changers (KUPVA), forex brokers, guarantee companies, financial leasing (non-bank), and other financial intermediaries. **Critical: the regulatory authority and licensing requirements depend entirely on which sub-activity you operate — OJK, Bank Indonesia (BI), or both.** Do not assume one regulator covers all activities under this code.
66199.whatYouNeed:
**Risk: Menengah Tinggi.** OSS Authority: **Menteri** — 7 working day Sertifikat Standar. But the sector-specific license from OJK or Bank Indonesia is the operative requirement.

**SUB-ACTIVITY MATRIX — choose your activity and its regulator:**

---

**ACTIVITY A — Payment Gateway / PJSP (Penyelenggara Jasa Sistem Pembayaran)**
Regulator: **Bank Indonesia (BI)**
- Izin: Izin PJSP under PBI No. 23/6/PBI/2021 (Sistem Pembayaran)
- Processing time: **6–12 months** (BI review)
- Modal minimum: varies by PJSP category:
  - Front-end (acquirer, payment initiation): IDR 3 miliar
  - Back-end (switching, clearing, settlement): IDR 50–100 miliar
- Indonesian data server mandatory (PP 71/2019)
- PJSP categories: Penyelenggara Infrastruktur SP (PISP), Penyelenggara Jasa Pembayaran (PJP)

**ACTIVITY B — E-Money Issuer (Uang Elektronik)**
Regulator: **Bank Indonesia (BI)**
- Izin: E-money license under PBI No. 20/6/PBI/2018
- Processing time: 6–12 months
- Modal minimum: IDR 3 miliar (untuk e-money dengan float < IDR 1 triliun)
- Server: must be in Indonesia
- Float management: e-money float must be placed in designated BI-approved bank accounts

**ACTIVITY C — Money Changer (KUPVA / Kegiatan Usaha Penukaran Valuta Asing)**
Regulator: **Bank Indonesia (BI)** (transferred from OJK for KUPVA in 2022)
- Izin: KUPVA license under PBI No. 18/20/PBI/2016
- Processing time: 3–6 months
- Modal minimum: IDR 100 juta (much lower than other activities)
- Physical premises required; signage and rate display regulations
- Bali: significant market — many hotel guests use money changers; illegal operators abound
- Forex report obligation: all transactions above USD 10,000 must be reported to PPATK

**ACTIVITY D — Forex Broker / Derivatives Trading**
Regulator: **OJK + Bappebti (Badan Pengawas Perdagangan Berjangka Komoditi)**
- Izin: Bappebti license for forex derivatives; OJK for securities-based forex
- Processing time: 6–12 months
- Highly restricted for foreign operators; retail forex margin trading is Bappebti territory

**ACTIVITY E — Guarantee Company (Perusahaan Penjaminan)**
Regulator: **OJK**
- Izin: OJK license under POJK 6/2020
- Modal minimum: IDR 100 miliar
- Processing time: 6–9 months

---

**Step-by-step for PT PMA payment gateway (Activity A — most common PMA path):**
1. **Establish PT PMA** — minimum capital according to PJSP category; notary deed, AHU (~4–6 weeks)
2. **NIB via OSS** — select 66199, Menengah Tinggi; 7 working days
3. **BI PJSP license application** — submit to BI Departemen Kebijakan Sistem Pembayaran; dossier includes business plan, IT architecture, data security audit, AML/CFT policy, escrow bank agreements
4. **Technology audit** — BI's IT assessors review platform; must meet PCI-DSS standards for card processing
5. **Minimum capital injection** — into Indonesian bank account
6. **BI approval + Izin PJSP** — issued after all assessments pass (6–12 months)
7. **Integration with National Payment Gateway** — SNAP (Standar Nasional Open API Pembayaran) compliance required
8. **Commence operations**

**PMA foreign ownership:** Terbuka — ownership percentage varies by activity and BI/OJK sub-regulation; payment gateways generally allow significant foreign ownership but BI regulation varies; confirm with BI before structuring.
66199.whatChanged: Code 66199 was updated in KBLI 2025 to reflect the broader digital financial services landscape that emerged post-2020. The most significant regulatory development: **Bank Indonesia's PBI 23/6/PBI/2021** restructured the entire payment system licensing framework, replacing the previous PJSP categories; KUPVA regulation was also updated. OJK and BI have increasingly clear demarcation of jurisdiction since the OJK Act amendment (UU 4/2023 — Penguatan dan Pengembangan Sektor Keuangan / P2SK Law), which transferred certain BI supervisory functions to OJK.

66301.whatItMeans: Investment fund management — managing mutual funds (reksa dana), discretionary portfolios, hedge funds, and other collective investment schemes on behalf of investors. The fund manager (Manajer Investasi / MI) makes investment decisions and earns a management fee on assets under management (AUM). Products: reksa dana saham (equity), reksa dana pendapatan tetap (fixed income), reksa dana campuran (balanced), reksa dana pasar uang (money market), reksa dana terproteksi (protected), ETF, and alternative investment funds. **Maximum foreign ownership: 99%** (OJK allows up to 99% but effectively requires at least one Indonesian director, per OJK regulation).
66301.whatYouNeed:
**Risk: Menengah Tinggi.** Authority: **Menteri** (OJK delegates to Menteri for NIB). OSS timeline 7 working days — but the OJK Manajer Investasi (MI) license is the critical gate (6–12 months additional).

**TWO-PHASE licensing — both mandatory:**

**PHASE 1 — OSS / NIB (7 working days):**
- Register PT (or PT PMA) on OSS, select 66301, Menengah Tinggi path
- NIB + Sertifikat Standar issued
- **Does NOT authorize fund management operations** — OJK license is required

**PHASE 2 — OJK Manajer Investasi License — 6–12 months:**
1. **Application to OJK** — Departemen Pengawasan Pasar Modal I (for securities-based funds) or IKNB (for other collective investment vehicles)
2. **Minimum paid-up capital:** IDR 25 miliar fully paid up at time of OJK application
3. **Tenaga Ahli requirement (MANDATORY):**
   - Minimum **2 Wakil Manajer Investasi (WMI)** — individuals holding valid WMI certification issued by OJK after passing WAPERD exam
   - At least 1 WMI must be a full-time director of the MI company
   - Preferred: CFA charterholder, CAIA, or equivalent international credential accepted by OJK
4. **Fit & proper test** — OJK vets all directors and commissioners
5. **Compliance infrastructure** — internal compliance function, risk management framework, investment committee structure
6. **SHAI system registration** — OJK's Sistem Hak Akses Investor; required for fund distribution
7. **Custodian bank agreement** — reksa dana assets must be held by a licensed custodian bank (OJK requirement)
8. **OJK Izin Usaha MI** — issued after all assessments pass
9. **Fund registration** — each reksa dana product requires separate OJK registration before launch

**To launch a listed ETF additionally:** BEI (Bursa Efek Indonesia) listing approval required.

**Step-by-step for PT PMA MI company:**
1. **Establish PT PMA** — minimum capital IDR 25B; 99% foreign allowed; recruit WMI-certified professionals in parallel (~4–6 weeks incorporation)
2. **Capital injection** — IDR 25B into Indonesian bank account
3. **NIB via OSS** — 66301, 7 working days
4. **OJK MI license application** — file complete dossier including business plan, investment methodology, compliance manual, custodian bank letter of intent (~6–12 months)
5. **OJK approval** — interview + document review
6. **Fund product registration** — register first fund with OJK (~2–4 months additional)
7. **Distribution agreement** — sign distribution agreements with bank or agent penjual (APERD) for fund sales
8. **Launch** — commence AUM generation

**Typical full timeline:** 12–20 months from incorporation to first fund launch.
**Minimum total capital:** IDR 25 miliar paid-up.
66301.whatChanged: Direct match from KBLI 2020 (MATCH_LANGSUNG). The OJK regulatory framework for Manajer Investasi was updated through OJK POJK 23/2016 and subsequent circulars. The key post-2020 development is OJK's push for ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) fund standards and the growth of OJK-licensed Reksa Dana ESG products — a genuine new product category for foreign MIs bringing ESG expertise.
66301.baliContext:
**📊 Fund Management in Bali — Boutique Opportunity Landscape**

**Why Bali for a boutique MI?**
- Bali's real estate and hospitality sector has a significant non-bank capital gap: villa developers, hotel owners, and eco-resort projects need equity/quasi-equity financing that neither banks nor P2P lenders provide
- A boutique Manajer Investasi can structure a Reksa Dana Penyertaan Terbatas (RDPT — limited participation private placement fund) targeting hospitality and real estate assets — legal framework exists under POJK 40/2015
- **Bali-themed ESG impact funds:** Blue economy (ocean conservation + sustainable fisheries), green hospitality (carbon-neutral resorts), Bali artisan livelihoods — these themes attract international impact investors and align with Bali's tourism brand

**The realistic market:**
- Most Indonesian MI companies are Jakarta-based and AUM-focused on conventional instruments (equities, bonds)
- A Bali-based boutique MI focusing on alternative and real assets with a clear ESG thesis has genuine differentiation
- Distribution challenge: retail fund sales require APERD network or bank distribution agreements; without these, you're in institutional/RDPT territory

**Required professionals in Bali:**
- WMI certificate holders are rare in Bali — most are in Jakarta; you will likely need to hire from Jakarta or sponsor WMI exam for local finance talent
- CFA and CAIA charterholders in Bali: handful; LinkedIn search + headhunter required

**⚠ Key Issues**
- **WMI certification is the long pole** — if your recruited WMI professionals aren't already certified, the WAPERD exam → OJK approval → WMI certificate process adds 3–6 months to your timeline
- **Custodian bank is mandatory** — reksa dana assets cannot be held by the MI itself; bank custody agreement is a prerequisite for OJK approval; negotiate before you apply
- **Each fund = separate OJK registration** — you cannot launch new products without a separate OJK approval per fund; plan a structured product pipeline
- **RDPT minimum investors:** A private placement fund (RDPT) requires maximum 100 investors (penyerta); each penyerta minimum IDR 5 miliar — this is institutional/HNWI territory only

- **Audited financials** — laporan keuangan audited by public accountant, with debt-to-equity ratios

**Authority chain:**
- **National:** Kementerian ATR/BPN (for KKPR), BKPM/OSS (for NIB)
- **Provincial:** Governor / DPMPTSP Provinsi
- **Local:** Bupati/Walikota — PP28 designates this level as primary licensing authority

**PMA:** Fully open (Terbuka) — 100% foreign ownership.

**⚠️ BALI GOVERNOR ALERT (Jan 2026):** The Governor of Bali has formally requested BKPM to CLOSE OSS registration for PMA companies operating Medium-Low risk (Menengah Rendah) activities in Bali — which directly includes 68111. This code is listed as the #1 most abused PMA code in Bali (Surat Gubernur B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP, 28 January 2026). If BKPM grants this request, new PMA companies will be UNABLE to register 68111 for Bali operations. Existing NIBs are expected to remain valid. Monitor OSS for changes.

68111.baliContext:

68112.whatItMeans: Leasing or renting out NON-RESIDENTIAL property that YOU OWN or lease — commercial spaces, offices, shops (toko), warehouses, industrial units, coworking spaces. This is for the LANDLORD/PROPERTY OWNER who rents out commercial property. NOT for tenants renting space, NOT for real estate agents (that's 68200). You own the building or hold the lease, and you rent it out to businesses. Excludes residential property (that's 68120).
68112.whatYouNeed:
**All scales (Mikro/Kecil/Menengah/Besar)**: Low risk (Rendah). NIB only, issued **automatically** (Otomatis) via OSS.

**Post-issuance obligations:**
- Submit periodic business activity reports (Laporan kegiatan usaha)

**Step-by-step to operate legally (PT PMA):**
1. **PT PMA incorporation** — notary deed, AHU registration, TDP (~2–4 weeks, IDR 8–15M notary fees)
2. **Property ownership/lease documentation** — PPJB (Perjanjian Pengikatan Jual Beli) or AJB (Akta Jual Beli) if you own; or long-term lease agreement (Hak Sewa) if you lease the property
3. **PBG (Persetujuan Bangunan Gedung)** — building permit must be valid for commercial use (not residential); verify zoning compliance (KKPR)
4. **NIB via OSS** — register on oss.go.id, select 68112, auto-issued (1–3 days)
5. **Rental agreements** — draft commercial lease contracts with tenants (notarized recommended)
6. **Tax compliance** — PPh Pasal 4(2) 10% final tax on rental income; PPN 11% if annual revenue > IDR 4.8B
7. **Ongoing compliance** — submit periodic reports, maintain PBG validity, renew property lease if applicable

**Typical total timeline:** 2–4 weeks (fastest property leasing path).
**Minimum PT PMA capital:** IDR 10 billion stated capital (Rp 2.5B paid-up).

**Authority:** OSS Pusat (central OSS system) — automatic issuance, no Bupati/Walikota review.
**PMA:** Fully open (Terbuka) — 100% foreign ownership. No local partner required.
68112.whatChanged: NEW code in KBLI 2025 — separates NON-RESIDENTIAL property leasing (68112) from RESIDENTIAL property leasing (68120). Previously both were lumped under a single code. This separation clarifies commercial vs. residential landlord activities. CRITICAL: 68112 is for the PROPERTY OWNER/LANDLORD, not for tenants or agents.
68112.baliContext:
**🏢 The Bali Commercial Property Market (Reality Check)**
- **Coworking spaces:** Canggu, Seminyak, Ubud — massive demand from digital nomads; spaces like Dojo Bali, Outpost, Tropical Nomad operate under 68112
- **Shop lots (toko):** Seminyak, Kuta, Ubud — retail spaces for F&B, fashion, wellness; rental rates IDR 50M–500M/year depending on location
- **Warehouses:** Mengwi, Tabanan — logistics, e-commerce fulfillment, manufacturing storage; growing demand from online retail boom
- **Office buildings:** Denpasar, Sanur — corporate offices, agency headquarters; rental rates IDR 200K–800K/m²/month
- Typical investment: IDR 5B–50B for commercial property acquisition or long-term lease (25–30 years Hak Sewa)
- Revenue model: Monthly/annual rent (IDR 20M–500M/month depending on size/location), service charges, utilities markup

---

**⚠ CRITICAL: 68112 Is for LANDLORDS, Not Tenants**
- **You are the PROPERTY OWNER** — you own the building or hold the long-term lease (Hak Sewa), and you rent it out
- **You are NOT the tenant** — if you're renting office space for your own business, you don't need 68112; your business uses its own KBLI code
- **You are NOT a real estate agent** — if you're intermediating property transactions for commission, you need 68200 (Real Estate Agency)
- **Example:**
  - PT PMA owns coworking building in Canggu, rents desks to freelancers = 68112 ✓
  - PT PMA rents office space for its own software development business = NO 68112 (use 62199 for software dev) ✗
  - PT PMA brokers commercial property deals for commission = 68200 (NOT 68112) ✗

---

**⚠ CRITICAL: Property Ownership Structure for PMA**
- **HGB (Hak Guna Bangunan) over HM (Hak Milik)** — most common structure for PMA in Bali
  - PT PMA holds HGB (building rights, 30+20 years renewable)
  - Land remains HM (freehold) owned by Indonesian citizen (WNI)
  - Notaris wajib — all HGB agreements must be notarized and registered at BPN (Badan Pertanahan Nasional)
- **Hak Sewa (Leasehold)** — alternative for PMA: long-term lease (25–30 years) from WNI landowner
  - Lower upfront cost than HGB
  - Renewal risk at end of lease term
  - Must be registered at notaris
- **Nominee arrangements** — ILLEGAL; BPN and PPATK (anti-money laundering) increased scrutiny since 2023

---

**⚠ CRITICAL: PBG Must Match Commercial Use**
- **PBG (Persetujuan Bangunan Gedung)** — building permit must specify commercial use (kantor, toko, gudang)
- **Common mistake:** Building has residential PBG, owner tries to rent as commercial space = zoning violation
- **KKPR (Kesesuaian Kegiatan Pemanfaatan Ruang)** — spatial conformity certificate from ATR/BPN; verify zoning allows commercial activity
- **Enforcement:** DPMPTSP Bali has increased inspections since 2024; non-compliant buildings face closure orders

---

**⚠ Common Mistakes in Bali Commercial Property Leasing**
- **Operating without NIB** — many small landlords rent out shop lots informally; PT PMA requires NIB for legal operation
- **Confusing 68112 with 68120** — commercial (68112) vs. residential (68120); different codes, different tax treatment
- **Mixing landlord activity with tenant activity** — if your PT PMA operates a business AND rents out space, you need BOTH codes (e.g., 68112 + 62199 for software dev)
- **Ignoring tax obligations** — PPh Pasal 4(2) 10% final tax on rental income is mandatory; PPN 11% if revenue > IDR 4.8B/year
- **Poor lease documentation** — commercial leases should be notarized; verbal agreements lead to disputes

69101.whatItMeans: Advocate activities — representing clients in court, appearing before judges and tribunals, preparing legal pleadings, and providing formal legal defense. This is courtroom lawyering in the traditional sense: litigation, criminal defense, civil lawsuits, arbitration hearings. 69101.whatYouNeed:
**WARNING: Effectively CLOSED to foreign investment.** While the KBLI data shows this as TERBUKA 100%, the Advocate Law (UU 18/2003) overrides this. Only Indonesian citizens who are registered members of PERADI (the Indonesian Bar Association) can practice as advocates. No foreign national — regardless of PMA structure — can appear in Indonesian courts.

**All scales (Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, Besar)**: Low risk (Rendah). NIB only, issued **automatically**.

**PMA:** The KBLI technically says open 100%, but this is misleading. Sector-specific legislation closes this to foreigners. Do NOT rely on the KBLI data alone — the Advocate Law is the binding constraint.
69101.whatChanged: Direct match from KBLI 2020 (MATCH_LANGSUNG). The code itself hasn't changed, and neither has the legal reality — Indonesia's advocacy profession has been closed to foreigners since the Advocate Law was enacted in 2003.
69101.baliContext: Foreign investors sometimes see this code's TERBUKA status and get excited. Don't. The Advocate Law is ironclad — no foreign citizen can practice as an advocate in Indonesia, full stop. If you need legal representation in Bali, you hire an Indonesian advocate. If you're a foreign lawyer wanting to work in Indonesia, look at 69102 (Legal Consultant) instead, which allows foreign firms to operate through Technical Assistance Agreements. Several international law firms have Bali-based consultants who advise on cross-border deals — but they cannot step into a courtroom.

69102.whatItMeans: Legal consulting — providing legal advice, contract drafting, corporate structuring, regulatory compliance guidance, and due diligence. Think corporate lawyers who never see a judge: they review contracts, advise on M&A, draft shareholder agreements, and navigate regulatory approvals.

You must operate through a Technical Assistance Agreement (TAA) with an Indonesian firm. The TAA structure means you partner with a local firm, provide international expertise, and share work. You can't just hang a shingle and start advising on Indonesian corporate law as a solo foreign entity.

71101.whatItMeans: This is your code for running an architecture practice — building design, town planning, landscape architecture. It covers the full spectrum from concept sketches to construction documentation. Because buildings involve public safety, this sits at Medium-High risk across all business scales, which means real licensing requirements beyond just your NIB.
71101.whatYouNeed:
**All scales (Mikro through Besar): Medium-High Risk**

You need an NIB plus a Sertifikat Standar (Standard Certificate) with verification. The big requirement here is your SBU (Sertifikat Badan Usaha) issued by an accredited LSBU — this is your company-level construction services license. Your professional staff must hold SKA (Sertifikat Keahlian) or SKK (Sertifikat Kompetensi Kerja) certifications.

For PMA companies, you'll likely need to register as a BUJKA (Badan Usaha Jasa Konstruksi Asing) — the foreign construction services entity framework.

**PMA: 100% foreign ownership allowed.**

---

### ⚠️ 2026 Regulatory Updates

**⚠️ SBU & BUJK Required:** Business Entity Certificate (SBU) and Construction License (BUJK) are mandatory. Requires demonstrated past project experience and significant net worth.
71101.whatChanged: Direct match from KBLI 2020 to 2025 — the code and scope remain the same. No structural changes, just the usual periodic review of risk classifications.
71101.baliContext:
Bali's building boom in hospitality and villa development means architecture firms stay busy, but local regulations are tightening around building heights, setbacks, and green zone compliance. You'll want staff who understand the Perda for each kabupaten, especially Badung and Gianyar where most development happens. Foreign architects often partner with locally-licensed firms to navigate the permit landscape faster.

---

**2026 Capital Update (BKPM 5/2025):** Paid-up capital reduced to **IDR 2.5 Billion** (~USD 150K). Total investment must still exceed IDR 10 Billion, but land and building values now count toward this threshold — a game-changer for Bali-based PT PMAs.
